analysis.title: A Trillion Dollar Math Glitch Emerges In The Heart Of The AI Bull Case
key_insights: Apollo chief economist Torsten Slok argues sell-side analyst forecasts for the AI ecosystem are internally inconsistent because analysts work in sector silos.
Tech-sector analysts expect sector operating cash flow to more than double to about $2.4 trillion by 2028, an increase of over $1.2 trillion.

Analysts covering the other S&P 500 sectors, which are tech's customers, expect those companies to add much less operating cash flow, so the tech forecast assumes demand that its customers' forecasts do not support.

Slok's conclusion: either tech's customers will generate a lot more cash than their analysts expect, or tech's cash flow forecasts are too optimistic, which raises the question of who will be paying for AI services.

Hyperscalers recently moved to negative free cash flow from capex. Forecasts have the group generating over $120B of FCF by 2030, while the article says maintenance capex on the data center buildout alone will reach $920B in a few years.

The article claims token prices have fallen sharply over the past three months as enterprise and retail customers move from frontier models to Chinese open-weight models. This is the author's assertion with no data cited.

Slok notes that heavy AI talk on earnings calls and in the media means companies are adopting it, hyping it for investors, or planning to use it to cut costs and jobs. The article says AI spending and measurable productivity gains have not yet materialized.
The article also points to circular financing in the AI ecosystem, cites a BIS warning this summer, and says off-balance-sheet obligations had grown to $3.1 trillion.

sector_views.rationale: Tech cash flow forecasts of about $2.4T by 2028 are not matched by customer-sector cash flow forecasts, so the author sees the AI bull case as overstated.

risk_factors: AI demand assumed in tech forecasts may not materialize if customer sectors do not generate matching cash flow.
Hyperscaler free cash flow is negative after the capex buildout, and maintenance capex is estimated at $920B in a few years.
Circular financing among AI companies, flagged by the BIS this summer.
Token price declines as customers shift to Chinese open-weight models, per the author.
AI hype running ahead of measurable spending and productivity gains.
cross_bank_references: Apollo's Torsten Slok: Wall Street equity analysts work in sector silos and fail to see the big picture.

tension_points.bull_case: Tech-sector analysts expect sector operating cash flow to more than double to about $2.4 trillion by 2028, and hyperscalers to reach over $120B of FCF by 2030.
tension_points.bear_case: Analysts covering tech's customers in other S&P 500 sectors expect much smaller cash flow gains, and maintenance capex alone is put at $920B, so the demand assumed by tech forecasts lacks a payer.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Tech's customers generate a lot more cash than their analysts currently expect.
